findings.title: Cache is not re-checked after acquiring the write lock
findings.body: The fast path reads entryPointAssetsCache under RLock, releases it, and then unconditionally takes the write Lock and reloads the manifest. If several requests arrive before the cache is populated (first load, or every request in dev mode), they all pass the RLock check and each performs the full file or CDN load, one after another. Re-checking entryPointAssetsCache after taking the write lock would let later callers reuse the result from the first one. In dev mode the reload is intentional, so the impact there is limited to the first-load case.

findings.title: Write lock is held across network I/O, blocking all readers
findings.body: entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock() is taken before readWebAssetsFromCDN(ctx, cdn) (line 56), which performs an HTTP GET via http.DefaultClient with no timeout of its own. While the CDN fetch is in flight, every other GetWebAssets call blocks on RLock at line 41, even if it would otherwise have been served from the cache. A slow or hanging CDN therefore stalls all page requests that call GetWebAssets. The lock should cover only the assignment to the global, or the fetch should be done outside the lock and the result stored afterwards.

findings.title: A failed reload overwrites the last good cache with nil
findings.body: On any error, result is nil and line 69 unconditionally executes entryPointAssetsCache = result. In dev mode, where the cache is reloaded on every call, a transient failure (for example a manifest being rewritten during a build) discards the previously valid assets, and the next call then fails too until the file is fixed. Storing the result only when err == nil would keep the last good value. The diff does not change this behaviour, but the locking refactor is the natural place to address it.

findings.title: No test covers concurrent access to the cache
findings.body: The PR is a data-race fix, but it adds no test that exercises GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines, such as a test run under go test -race. Without one, the fix cannot be verified and regressions to the locking will not be caught.
